question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=({x}^{3}-2x){e}^{{x}^{4}+5x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the product rule for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{3}-2x){e}^{{x}^{4}+5x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}-2x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{{x}^{4}+5x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}-2x)+{x}^{4}+5x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}-2x)+{x}^{4}+5x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\frac{3{x}^{2}-2}{{x}^{3}-2x}+4{x}^{3}+5 \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{3{x}^{2}-2}{{x}^{3}-2x}+4{x}^{3}+5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{3{x}^{2}-2}{{x}^{3}-2x}+4{x}^{3}+5)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=({x}^{3}-2x){e}^{{x}^{4}+5x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =({x}^{3}-2x){e}^{{x}^{4}+5x}(\frac{3{x}^{2}-2}{{x}^{3}-2x}+4{x}^{3}+5) \\  & ={e}^{{x}^{4}+5x}[3{x}^{2}-2+(4{x}^{3}+5)({x}^{3}-2x)] \\  & ={e}^{{x}^{4}+5x}(4{x}^{6}-8{x}^{4}+5{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}-10x-2)\end{aligned}
$$
